assertions.name: residual_bracketed_by_consecutive_odd_powers_under_convention_D
assertions.source: EXPECTED RED, and red is the result. Convention D gives h*z^3 = 2.755 deg < h*z^2 = 4.496 deg, and the observed 2.1 deg is BELOW that window. The 1.49/2.99 deg figures this assertion quoted until 2026-08-23 are convention C. Do not relax this gate: it records that the bracket argument does not survive the canonical convention. Note also that the premise fails independently — h*z^k is odd-in-h only if z is bar-even, and z_D is not.

description: H2S +2.1 deg chiral-residue parity check, convention D. The block's identification of the residual as the bar-ANTI-symmetric (odd-in-h) channel rests on a bracket h*z^3 < 2.1 < h*z^2. That bracket is a CONVENTION-C fact: in C it is 1.49 < 2.1 < 2.99 (true), in the canonical D it is 2.75 < 2.1 < 4.50 (false, 2.1 is below the window). Worse, the parity premise itself fails under D — h*z^k is odd-in-h only if z is bar-even, and z_D(1/q)/z_D(q) = q^-4, so the classification is unavailable rather than merely unfavourable. And even under C the window is 71% of the target, so nearly any residual would have passed it. The assertion below is red and is correct to be red; do not relax it. The H2O-clean / H2S-residual dichotomy is untouched by this — only this bracket argument for it is.

data.finding: The H2O-clean / H2S-residual DICHOTOMY (two self-dual lone pairs vs a self-dual 3s^2 plus a chiral 3p_z) is a structural reading and is not touched here. What is retracted is the quantitative parity argument offered for it: (b) the bar-parity classification of h*z^k does not exist under convention D, since z_D(1/q)/z_D(q) = q^-4 exactly, so the product has no clean bar-parity; and (a) this particular bracket does not contain 2.1 deg under D. Even under C the bracket spanned 71% of the target, so it distinguished almost nothing. Neither point excludes the +2.1 deg being chiral by another route -- only this construction.
